body:
Three documents are on the table — the account, the objection, and the rival — and they converge more than they first appear to. My decisions, stated up front: I use the objection's order-of-operations criticism and the rival's probe; I revise the account's central mechanism rather than discard it; I reject the remedy-first sequence and the demotion of the avoidance to a mere symptom; and I leave open which of the three readings of the disputes is actually true.

The convergence: the objection's distinction between memorial and normative disagreement and the rival's scope-ambiguity reading are the same point at different depths, and the account's own example supports the critics' version better than its own. 'I'll do the dishes' covering different amounts of work under different schedules is not forgetting; it is ambiguity exposed by changed circumstances. The account's retrospective claim (agreements drifted because nothing fixed their content) is supported by the material; its prospective claim (recording them now will stop the drift) is not, and the objection is right that these must be held apart. I therefore revise the mechanism to: underspecification at the moment of agreement, with schedule change doing the exposing.

What survives the revision is the account's practical insight that terms need to become explicit; what changes is where the explicitness goes. The first fix is stating scope at the moment of agreement — 'when I say dishes this week, I mean these tasks, by this day, and then we re-agree' — not writing things down afterward. This move costs nothing, presupposes no diagnosis, and requires no one's buy-in: the person asking can begin it unilaterally this week for their own commitments, whatever the household later decides.

The next step is the rival's probe, which I adopt because it is the only proposal on the table that responds to all three readings at once. Ask each flatmate separately what they thought a specific past agreement meant — framed as mapping present divergence, not adjudicating the past, since recollection is the disputed faculty and the probe only reaches what each person now reports. Its outcomes should be pre-specified so the answers are not retrofitted: if reports cluster around scope, recurrence, or timing, the underspecification reading gains and the fix is narrow (scope-stating, with a minimal note only if needed); if they do not cluster, the recording and ambiguity readings weaken and the standing-negotiation reading gains relative weight — by elimination only, which is weak evidence and should not be overread; and if the avoidant friend declines even this one question, that refusal is itself evidence for the avoidance-as-central reading and routes the next move.

The approach to the friend should be routed by the probe, not run in parallel with a fixed framing. I accept the rival's reframing — 'I want to hear how the group conversations look from your side' rather than 'why have you been avoiding them' — and its caution that a private approach can reproduce the group dynamic at smaller scale; the account was wrong to present the one-to-one as clearly correct. If the friend answers the probe, the one-to-one has a natural occasion; if they decline, the thing to name is the avoidance itself, possibly at group level, before any system is proposed.

What I reject: the written record plus weekly check-in as the first move, because — as the account itself conceded before the objection made it load-bearing — the remedy presupposes the conversation the avoidance puts in question; the demotion of avoidance to symptom, which the material does not license, though I equally do not affirm the objection's inversion as fact; and any present ranking of mediator, reassignment, or formalization, which none of the documents can support. The record remains held as a conditional later step, with pre-specified markers: if it is tried and disputes move onto the record (who wrote it, what 'done' means, who is on it), the rival's relocation worry is confirmed and counts against extending the system; a quiet week counts as uninformative in either direction, as both critics insisted.

One tension I owe the objection: its sharpened self-falsifier — arguments persisting after a record with 'done' defined would tell against its own ordering — still requires running the record, which its order-of-operations argument defers. The probe-first sequence serves both halves: it delays the trigger without discarding the test. Left open: which reading is true; whether the avoidance predates the schedule change, on which the account and the objection silently disagree; and the standing-negotiation reading, which no instrument currently proposed can test directly. What to do this week: state scope for your own agreements, and ask the probe question of each flatmate — nothing more formal until those return.
commitments:
The strongest thing I commit to is a claim: the revision of the account's mechanism from memory failure to underspecification at the moment of agreement. Its grounds are internal — the account's own dish example — and it can fail. If the probe shows the flatmates recall identical scope and still dispute fairness or timing, or if scope-stating is tried and changes nothing, the underspecification reading weakens and the memorial or normative readings regain ground; I would count that against my revision, not as noise.

Behind that sits an interpretive claim about the exposed texts: that the objection's memorial/normative distinction and the rival's scope-ambiguity reading are the same point. My revision's grounding partly depends on that identification; a reader who rejects it weakens but does not destroy the revision, since the dish example supports it independently.

The probe is a proposed application, and I inherit the rival's caveat: it reaches present reports, not the agreed past, and it can be heard as interrogation. I commit to the branch discipline stated in the body — in particular to reading non-clustering as weak, eliminative evidence for the standing-negotiation reading and nothing stronger, and to counting the friend's refusal of the probe as evidence for the avoidance reading rather than explaining it away as resistance.

My rejection of the remedy-first order is a criticism of sequencing that depends on the objection's order-of-operations argument; if that argument is defeated — for instance, if the avoidance proves recent and slight and both other flatmates actively want a written system — the rejection weakens and the record could move earlier. The criticism and its grounds stand apart from the record's possible later use, which I still hold open under the pre-specified markers (relocation onto the note, quiet week uninformative); if a trial runs, I commit to honoring those markers rather than retrofitting an interpretation.

The unilateral scope-stating move is a proposed action with low but nonzero risk — it could be experienced as pedantry or as unilateral rule-setting — and I would drop it if it generates friction rather than clarity.

Unresolved problems: I cannot say which reading of the household is true, whether the avoidance predates the schedule changes (a chronology the account and the objection quietly treat differently), or how the standing-negotiation reading could ever be tested directly; and I mention mediator and reassignment only as unrankable alternatives on which nothing here depends. If the inquiry continues, what I propose to take up is formulating the probe question so it is not heard as interrogation, revising the branch interpretations if the probe returns something no branch anticipated, and drawing the observation list for a record trial if the household reaches one.
